newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases on dollar covering, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases on dollar covering, seen in range.

text.p: * Ringgit eases on short covering of dollar
* Dollar/ringgit seen in range ahead of FOMC meeting
The ringgit fell from its opening level against the dollar in early Asian trading as offshore players covered short dollar/ringgit positions.
Dealers said trading was much calmer compared with a 250-point fluctuation on Friday.
The ringgit fell to a low of 2.4945/55 a dollar from its opening of 2.4850/60. It was quoted at 2.4930/40 at 0200 GMT.
"Dollar/ringgit is quiet this morning and I think it'll be rangy for the day," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
He said tomorrow/next on the ringgit has fallen back to near normal levels, and this should calm the market.

Tom/next was trading as high as 300 on Friday after talk that Bank Negara had told local banks to stop quoting tom/next to offshore players, causing heavy unwinding of long dollar/ringgit positions. Bank Negara denied it had issued instructions to banks to stop undertaking swap transactions.
Dealers said they expected thin trading due to market holidays in several European centres today and ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
They said foreign funds were still trying to get out of their positions and the dollar would be sold on any rallies against the ringgit.

"We should see a lot of dollar selling at between 2.4950 and 2.5000. With interbank rates still high, it will be too expensive for players to maintain short ringgit positions," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He expects immediate support for the ringgit at 2.4980.
Short-term interbank rates have risen sharply due to a liquidity squeeze.
